subject: Service availability exception request and monthly credit guardrails
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@tritondata.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Katie Lee <katie.lee@tritondata.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SLA template: request for availability exception + credit cap

Marcus —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Triton is excited about Redwood’s latency profile, but our legal team needs one carve-out in the SLA for our initial private deployment: because we are integrating a legacy on-prem telemetry adapter, we cannot guarantee the standard 99.95% uptime in month one.

Specifically, we’d like to request an "initial deployment exception" setting the month-1 uptime target to 98.5% (we expect to reach 99.9% by month 3). We also need an explicit cap on monthly service credits not to exceed 20% of our monthly committed fees for the first three months.

I attached a short note with the request and a proposed language block (Triton_SLA_Request_v1.pdf). Can you let me know if Redwood can accept this as a temporary exception or propose alternatives?

Appreciate a quick turnaround — our procurement committee meets on Thursday.

— Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Platform, Triton Dataworks
samir.patel@tritondata.com
+1 415 555 0198

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@tritondata.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA template: request for availability exception + credit cap

Samir —

Thanks for the clear ask and the attached language. Short answer: we’re open to an initial deployment exception, but we have two concerns to balance: (1) fairness to other customers and (2) our ops and escalation economics if availability drops below expectations.

Next steps I propose:
- Internal review with Legal & Product (looping Karthik and Laura) to propose a controlled exception term.
- Counterproposal: a month-1 availability floor of 98.5% as you requested, with credits calculated per our standard table but with a temporary cap of 30% of monthly committed fees for month 1 only (rather than 20%).
- Commit to a phased remediation plan (tickets, runbook handoff, weekly sync) that we’ll include in the MOP to ensure we hit 99.9% by month 3.

I’ve asked Karthik to weigh in on legal-side constraints; Laura will coordinate SRE operational guarantees. If you can confirm the procurement timing, we’ll aim to turn a redline by Wednesday EOD.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
+1 650 555 0123

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T14:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA template: request for availability exception + credit cap

Marcus / team —

I reviewed Triton’s requested language. High level: we can accept a limited exception but need to (A) cap the exception duration, (B) ensure credits remain a meaningful incentive, and (C) add an exclusion for outages caused by Triton-managed network/adapter changes. Proposed constraints:
- Exception term: Month 1 only, expires at end of billing month 1.
- Cap on credits: 30% of monthly fees for month 1 (we can consider 25% if Triton accepts a stronger remediation timeline).
- Exclusions: scheduled maintenance, customer third-party adapter issues, and force majeure.
- Acceptance criteria: measurable remediation milestones (SRE runbook handoff and two-week stability gate).

I’ll draft redline language for Marcus to send externally. Ben — can you confirm we can deliver the operational runbook and weekly status report commitment?

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Counsel, Contracts, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T08:17:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA template: request for availability exception + credit cap

Confirm — we can provide:
- An onboarding runbook (attachment: RDW-SLA-Redline-triton-v2.pdf will include the runbook summary)
- Weekly status updates for 90 days, with an escalation contact and 4-hour incident acknowledgement SLO for Sev-1 incidents during the exception window

I also suggest we include a post-mortem commitment for any Sev-1 during month 1. That gives Triton transparency and reduces negotiation friction.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@tritondata.com>
Cc: Katie Lee <katie.lee@tritondata.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T10:42:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed redline for Triton initial-deployment exception (attached)

Samir —

Thanks for the patience. Attached is our proposed redline that captures the exception language and operational commitments (RDW-SLA-Redline-triton-v2.pdf). Summary of key points:
- Month 1 uptime floor: 98.5%.
- Credit calculation: standard SLA table applies; credit payout subject to a month-1 cap of 30% of monthly committed fees.
- Exception expires end of month 1; automatic reversion to standard SLA thereafter.
- Exclusions: customer-managed adapter outages, scheduled maintenance with 48h notice, and third-party network outages.
- Operational commitments: onboarding runbook handoff, weekly status reports, 4-hour Sev-1 acknowledgment, and post-mortem obligation for Sev-1 incidents.

If Triton agrees, we’ll draft the formal amendment and get legal sign-off. If you prefer a 25% cap in exchange for an explicit bi-weekly engineering workshop in month 1, we can pivot there.

Can you confirm by Wednesday morning to meet your procurement window?

— Marcus

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@tritondata.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Katie Lee <katie.lee@tritondata.com>
Date: 2026-11-04T15:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed redline for Triton initial-deployment exception (attached)

Marcus / team —

Appreciate the fast turnaround. Triton’s legal reviewed the redline overnight. We can accept the 30% month-1 cap if Redwood will add: (1) an explicit 2-week engineering workshop during month 1 (remote calls + shared backlog) and (2) a rollback trigger clause: if uptime stays below 98.0% for any 7-day window in month 1, we retain the right to pause traffic to the private integration until the cause is remediated.

Katie and I are OK to proceed if you can confirm those two additions; procurement will sign the amendment once we have those bullets in writing.

If you prefer, I can mark up the PDF and send it back.

— Samir
thread_notes: Marcus to confirm feasibility of 2-week workshop and rollback trigger; legal will prepare final amendment. Awaiting Marcus reply before final sign.
